name: Differential_Equation_1
questiontext:
Solve the following differential equation: \[ {{CT:0}}\frac{dy}{d{{CT:0}}} + {{CT:1}}{{CT:0}}+{{CT:2}} = 0. \] Use the letter "c" (small case) to denote the arbitrary constant occuring in the general solution.
\(y({{CT:0}})\) =[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: For the equation \[ {{CT:0}}\frac{dy}{d{{CT:0}}} + {{CT:1}}{{CT:0}}+{{CT:2}} = 0 \] rearranging gives \[dy = \frac{(-{{CT:1}}{{CT:0}}-{{CT:2}})}{{CT:0}}d{{CT:0}}\] Therefore \[\int dy = \int\frac{(-{{CT:1}}{{CT:0}}-{{CT:2}})}{{CT:0}}d{{CT:0}} =\int(-{{CT:1}}-\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:0}})d{{CT:0}}\] Hence \[y = {{CT:3}}\]

on_true.feedback: Your answer may satisfy the differential equation, but either is mathematically incorrect (look especially at the integral of 1/f(x)), has no constant or has used a different constant than "c".
